You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC demo discipline

## Workflow
1. Parse each region, background, object colors, divider orientation, and dimensions from the current instance. Treat task IDs and remembered task-specific rules as hypotheses only; recurring tasks may vary in geometry and palette.
2. Compare every demo input-output pair cell-by-cell. Identify equality/inequality mappings, output palette, row/column orientation, and unchanged cases. Explain all observations with one consistent rule before submitting.
3. Choose demos by information value. If candidate rules remain ambiguous and a wrong submission costs more than a demo, request a demo that distinguishes them. Do not spend attempts on speculative palette or orientation variants.

Before a later submission, verify each output coordinate, dimensions, and palette against the rule and examples.
5. Maintain the interface contract on every turn: output exactly one valid JSON action object on the final line, with no explanation or extra text. Valid actions are `submit`, `request_demos`, or `finish` only when the instance is over. Do not use `finish` prematurely.

Demo 1: bg8, 4-frame interior 2x2 ->2; 0-frame 4x4->2; 0-frame 6x6->2; 9-frame singleton marker ->7. Demo 2: 9-frame 2x2->2, 8-frame 4x5->7, 1-frame 3x3->7. Demo 3: 9-frame 2x2->2 and 8-frame 2x2->2. Demo 4: 3-frame 4x4->2; 6-frame 2x2->2; 8-frame singleton->7. Test features (0-indexed): frame color1 rows0-2 cols19-21, singleton center (1,20); frame color1 rows4-11 cols10-17 with strict interior rows5-10 cols11-16 (6x6 blank); frame color4 rows4-8 cols22-26, interior rows5-7 cols23-25 (3x3 blank); frame color6 rows10-12 cols0-2, singleton center (11,1); frame color9 rows11-13 cols5-7, singleton center (12,6); frame color3 rows10-13 cols22-25, interior rows11-12 cols23-24 (2x2 blank). Eight rejected outputs all preserved shapes and variously filled subsets with 2 and/or 7; no rule obtained. Rejected variants largely assigned broad 2 to large blank spaces and 7 to singleton markers, changing which objects were filled. Do not repeat these assumptions/guesses. Main unresolved anomaly: demo2 blank 4x5 ->7 while other blank regions including 4x4, 2x2, 6x6 ->2. Could be relation to frame color/shape/context, not solely area or interior content. Need a demo varying one factor, especially blank 4x5 vs other sizes or same outline color with different dimensions, to resolve. Preserve uncertainty; don't make blind palette variants.

### Solved 11x18 instance: recolor all closed frame interiors by area parity
Preserve frame borders and exterior/background. Fill every strict rectangular interior: odd number of interior cells -> color 7; even number -> color 2. Demos confirmed 1x1, 3x3, 5x5 interiors -> 7; 2x2, 4x4, 6x6 -> 2. The proven invariant is interior-cell-count parity; observed interiors happened to be squares.

Solved test had THREE frames, including an easy-to-miss large color-3 frame: color-5 frame rows1-3, cols0-2 had 1x1 interior at (2,1) ->7; color-8 frame rows6-9, cols1-4 had 2x2 interior rows7-8, cols2-3 ->2; color-3 frame rows0-7, cols6-13 had 6x6 interior rows1-6, cols7-12 ->2. All other cells/borders unchanged. Accepted output was submitted in this session.

Failure lesson: the first three rejected submissions omitted the large frame's 6x6 interior (and varied fills on the two small interiors). The successful submission recolored all three. Always scan the entire grid for every enclosed frame, including large ones; do not stop after the obvious small objects. Historical task notes can conflict across recurrences; the above is confirmed for this instance by the demos and accepted answer.
A current 28x23 instance contains outlined rectangles with interiors: color-0 outline at rows 8-11, cols 7-10 (2x2 interior); color-3 outline rows 9-11 cols 17-19 (1x1 interior); color-4 outline rows 14-20 cols 15-21 (5x5 interior); color-5 outlines rows 17-20 cols 0-3 (2x2), rows 16-19 cols 5-8 (2x2), rows 18-20 cols 11-13 (1x1); color-8 outline rows 22-24 cols 12-14 (1x1). Earlier memory says dimension-based recoloring, but submissions applying 1x1->7, 2x2->2, 5x5->2 or background were rejected repeatedly. Six demos in that run established only varying interior fills, not a stable size rule: demo1 2x2 interior -> 7, 6x6 ->2; demo2 2x2 ->7, 2x2 ->7, 1x1->7, 3x3->2, 3x3->7; demo3 4x4->2, 3x3->7, 1x1->7; demo4 3x3->7, 6x6->2, 2x2->2; demo5 3x3->7 and 1x1->7; demo6 6x6->2 and 4x4->2. Do not repeat a size-only palette rule. Request demos and compare rectangle outline color, interior size, location/context, and neighboring shapes; preserve outlines/background.

## Paired-band comparison pattern
When a solid full-width row or full-height column separates two aligned bands, exclude the divider and compare corresponding cells. A common learned mapping is equality => 3 and inequality => the first band's background; determine that background from the full band rather than assuming its most visually prominent color. Horizontal divider: compare upper/lower bands; vertical divider: compare left/right. Confirm the exact palette and mapping from current demos rather than importing this pattern blindly.

## Pitfalls
- A known task ID or memory is not a substitute for current demo evidence.

- A rejection is evidence; change the rule/model, not merely the output's appearance.
